sections.html:
Holladay lies in the center of Salt Lake County, almost wholly homes, with Murray, Millcreek and Cottonwood Heights around it and the Wasatch National Forest on its eastern edge. The 2020 count came to 31,965 residents in 11,814 households and 12,368 housing units, of which about 4.5% stood empty. Few homes sit vacant here, which keeps competition for well-kept houses steady.

The city spans three ZIP codes: 84117, 84121 and 84124. Your mailing ZIP may differ from a neighbor's two streets away, so read the one on the county parcel record before signing.

Permits are required here for additions, remodels of any size, basement finishes, reroofing, solar, pools, spas and front-yard fencing. Staff check plans against current codes first, and a Certificate of Occupancy comes after final inspections.

A few jobs are exempt: decks lower than 18 inches above grade, backyard fences up to 6 feet, like-for-like swaps of plumbing fixtures, lights and receptacles, plus cabinets, trim, carpet and paint. A detached shed of 200 square feet or less and under 20 feet tall needs no building permit but does get a zoning check.

  • Tree removal on public or private property can require a permit under city code sections 13.77.080 and 13.77.090.
  • Fences in a front yard are capped at 4 feet, while side and rear yards go to 6 feet.
  • After a violation, a Correction Notice generally gives about 30 days to cure it.
  • Each subdivision's association enforces its own covenants, not the city planning office.

Holladay was a county community until 1999, so a house remodeled before then can have an odd permit history. Phone Community Development at 801-527-3890 to learn whether an older addition or basement finish has a closed permit. Fence doubts go to a surveyor, since the city does not mark property lines.

sections.h2: Selling a house with unpermitted work
sections.html: A basement or addition built without a permit will not block a cash sale, though the price may reflect it. Many bank-financed deals fall apart over it, since appraisers and lenders want to know what is legal. If you list with an agent instead, plan on closing out the work with the building office first.

Holladay belongs to the Granite School District, and Olympus High School is the one public high school within city limits. Assignments follow district boundary maps, so look up your address on the district site.

The county, not the city, assesses, collects and records.

The old Cottonwood Mall site near 4800 S. Highland Drive is now Holladay Hills, a large mixed development with apartments and townhomes, some of them listed at $1 million or more. Someone touring an older house is often also touring a new townhome, which pushes the older one to win on lot, location or condition. If yours needs work, an as-is sale avoids the contest.

The Wasatch fault, Utah's most active, runs along the Wasatch Front, and the Utah Geological Survey publishes liquefaction maps for these valleys. Exposure varies by lot, and the maps show only broad patterns, so a specific lot needs its own report from a qualified engineer and geologist.

Older masonry draws the most questions. Unreinforced brick built from roughly the 1920s to the 1960s was not designed for sideways ground motion, so expect an interested buyer of such a house to ask about bracing and chimney anchors.

Holladay property tax is billed by Salt Lake County: the whole year is payable by November 30, and any balance left after that is delinquent from December 1.

Tax stepTimingWho handles it
Valuation dateJanuary 1County assessor
Valuation notices outJuly and AugustCounty assessor
Appeal windowJuly 31 to September 15Board of Equalization
Tax notices outBy November 1County treasurer
Last day without penaltyNovember 30County treasurer

Appeals cover this year's market value only, and they need proof: a recent purchase, an appraisal, or at least three comparable sales. The Treasurer's office, at 385-468-8300, also takes applications for tax relief programs. Details are on the Salt Lake County tax administration page.

Because the primary residential exemption removes 45%, a main residence is taxed on 55% of market value. A buyer must file a new claim after purchase, and skipping it can mean tax on the full value that year. A house you rented out has its own declaration process.

sections.h2: How a cash sale closes and what gets recorded
sections.html:
Cash deals here close at a title or escrow company, which sends the deed to the Salt Lake County Recorder. No lender means no appraisal contingency and no loan approval holding things up.

Recording costs a flat $40. Each document needs a Salt Lake County legal description, the parcel number, an original notarized signature and the buyer's mailing address. Staff there will not draft, notarize or provide forms, and originals come back by mail roughly two to three weeks after imaging. The number for questions is 385-468-8145.

  • Start the title search sooner if the house passed through a family trust or an estate.
  • Make sure names on the deed agree with the signature page and the notary block.
  • Have the title officer split the year's tax between you and the buyer.

At signing you meet the title officer, go over the settlement figures and sign. The title company then records the deed and pays you. Any mortgage payoff or tax balance is deducted first. You do not stage the house, host an open house or repair what an inspector might flag.

sections.h2: Your options as a Holladay seller
sections.html:
You can hire an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. A listing means cleaning, repairs and showings against new townhome competition; a cash offer takes the house untouched.

  • Inherited houses that need upkeep, often in older neighborhoods.
  • Rentals with tenants living there, which are hard to show.
  • Homes where a basement or addition went in without a permit.
  • Owners behind on payments who want a dependable closing date.

Weigh any offer against what a listing would leave you after repairs, commission and carrying costs. Get the closing date and proof of funds in writing.

Before you decide, gather the deed, your latest tax notice, any permit records and a payoff statement if a mortgage remains. Those papers let a buyer price the house accurately and let the title company spot problems early. If the house sits in a trust or an estate, bring the trust documents or court papers too, so everyone who must sign is identified before the closing date is set.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Holladay house with an unpermitted basement?
faqs.a: Yes, a cash buyer can take it as is, though the price may reflect the missing permit. Lenders often object, so a listing may mean closing out the work with the Holladay building office first.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Holladay home?
faqs.a: November 30, billed through the Salt Lake County Treasurer, with delinquency from December 1. A mid-year sale is usually settled by splitting the bill at closing.

faqs.q: Does the new owner keep my primary residential exemption?
faqs.a: No. A buyer has to apply with the county, and a missed filing can mean tax on the full market value for that year.

faqs.q: How long does recording the deed take in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: The title company normally submits it right after closing, and the county mails originals back about two to three weeks after imaging.

faqs.q: Is Holladay in a liquefaction or fault zone?
faqs.a: Only a lot-by-lot review can say. The Utah Geological Survey maps liquefaction and fault hazards along the Wasatch Front, and one property calls for a site-specific study by a qualified professional.
